gaps.sentence: My grandmother goes to ___ church every morning before work.
gaps.explanation: 'Go to church' (as worshipper) takes no article; 'the church' would mean the building.

gaps.sentence: He was wearing ___ strange metal bracelet on his left wrist.
gaps.explanation: 'A strange bracelet' (first mention); body parts after prepositions traditionally take 'the' (on the left wrist).

gaps.sentence: We bought ___ antique mirror at the flea market.
gaps.explanation: 'An antique mirror' — 'antique' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: His mother went to ___ prison to visit him.
gaps.explanation: Visitors go to the building: 'went to the prison'.

gaps.sentence: We had ___ wonderful time in Prague.
gaps.explanation: 'Have a wonderful/great/good time' — 'time' here is countable and takes 'a'.

gaps.sentence: We stayed at ___ hotel right next to the station.
gaps.explanation: 'The station' — in a town there is usually one known station; context makes it definite.

gaps.sentence: ___ unemployment has fallen sharply this year.
gaps.explanation: Unemployment as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: He joined ___ army when he was eighteen.
gaps.explanation: Institutions take 'the': the army, the police, the church.
